title: Concurrent retries can queue duplicate send tasks
reasoning: The command reads failed promos, then later changes each row to DRAFT and queues a task without an atomic conditional transition. Two overlapping invocations can both observe the same FAILED row before either save completes and both enqueue send_promo_email_task for the same promo. The same race exists for the --promo-id path because it fetches and saves without checking the status at update time.
reproduction: Start two retry_failed_emails commands at the same time against the same FAILED PromoEmail. Both can load the row while it is FAILED and both can call send_promo_email_task.delay for the same id.
recommendation: Use a transaction with select_for_update, or perform a conditional update such as filtering by id and status=FAILED and only enqueue when exactly one row was transitioned. For batch retries, claim rows atomically before queueing tasks.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests exercise overlapping command invocations or verify that a failed promo is only queued once under concurrent retry attempts.
suggestedRegressionTest: Simulate two concurrent retry attempts for the same FAILED PromoEmail and assert only one transition succeeds and only one task is enqueued.
minimumFixScope: Change retry_failed_emails.py so both single-id and batch retry paths atomically claim FAILED rows before enqueueing Celery tasks.
